items.label: list_item
items.text: 3An important stage in the Contact process for the production of sulfuric acid involves a reversible reaction:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 S O _ { 2 } ( g ) + O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightleftharpoons 2 S O _ { 3 } ( g ) \quad \Delta H = - 1 9 6 k J / m o l

items.label: text
items.text: At 450 °C the reaction mixture consists of a dynamic equilibrium involving sulfur dioxide, oxygen and sulfur trioxde.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Explain what is meant by the term dynamic equilibrium. Be sure that you have explained what both of the words mean.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Predict and explain the effect of an increase in pressure on the proportion of the sulfur trioxide present in the equilibrium mixture.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Predict and explain the effect of lowering the temperature of the mixture on the position of equilibrium of the reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: 4Hydrogen can be made by the reaction between methane (natural gas) and steam. The reaction can be carried out by passing a mixture of methane and steam over a nickel catalyst at pressures between 2 and 30 atmospheres and a temperature of about 1000 °C.

items.label: formula
items.text: C H _ { 4 } ( g ) + H _ { 2 } O ( g ) \rightleftharpoons C O ( g ) + 3 H _ { 2 } ( g ) \quad \Delta H = + 2 1 0 k J / m o l

items.label: list_item
items.text: a The pressure used is relatively low. What would be the effect on the conversion of the methane into carbon monoxide and hydrogen if the pressure was higher?

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Explain why a high temperature is used to get a good conversion of methane into hydrogen.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Explain the use of the nickel catalyst in the production of hydrogen, referring to both the rate of the reaction and the position of equilibrium.

items.label: list_item
items.text: 5 Ammonia, NH3, is manufactured by passing a mixture of nitrogen and hydrogen over an iron catalyst at a pressure of 200 atmospheres or more, and a temperature of 450 °C.

items.label: formula
items.text: N _ { 2 } ( g ) + 3 H _ { 2 } ( g ) \equiv 2 N H _ { 3 } ( g ) \quad \Delta H = - 9 2 k J / m o l

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Explain why this reaction will produce a higher percentage conversion into ammonia if the pressure is very high.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b 200 atmospheres is a high pressure, but not very high. Give a reason why most ammonia manufacturers don't use a pressure of, for example, 1000 atmospheres. (Hint: think about the risk of using high pressure.)

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Predict and explain whether you would get the best yield of ammonia in the equilibrium mixture at a low or a high temperature.

items.label: list_item
items.text: d The temperature used, 450 °C, is neither very high nor very low. Suggest a reason why a manufacturer might choose a temperature which gave less than an ideal percentage conversion. (Hint: think about rates of reaction.)
